pl-l4d48c5-d1e115.summary: States that when the Lord comes to judgment in great power, the sun and moon are said to be darkened not by loss of their light but by the brightness of a greater light coming upon them; the powers of heaven, the angels, are said to be moved not by fear of damnation but by wonder at what they see.
claims: The heavenly bodies are outshone, not extinguished.
The angels are moved by wonder.

pl-l4d48c5-d1e121.summary: Cites Job: the pillars of heaven tremble at his coming.

pl-l4d48c5-d1e127.summary: States that before the day of judgment the sun and moon will suffer eclipse, as Joel says: the sun will be turned to darkness and the moon to blood before the great and terrible day of the Lord, great for the great things done in it.
claims: Sun and moon will be eclipsed before the judgment.

pl-l4d48c5-d1e134.summary: States that when the new heaven and new earth are made, the moon's light will be as the sun's and the sun's sevenfold, as Isaiah says, that is as in the seven days of creation before the first man's sin, since the light of sun, moon, and stars was lessened by that sin; then the sun will receive the reward of its labor, shining sevenfold, and there will be no alternation of day and night, but only day.
claims: The heavenly lights were lessened by sin and will be restored.
After the judgment there will be only day.

pl-l4d48c5-d1e146.summary: Cites Zechariah: there will be one day known to the Lord, neither day nor night, and at evening there will be light; since there will be no alternation of day and night, but continual day and light.

pl-l4d48c5-d1e155.summary: Notes that Isaiah seems to say sun and moon will not then shine, speaking to the blessed: you will no longer have the sun for light by day, nor will the moon's brightness illumine you, but the Lord will be your everlasting light.

pl-l4d48c5-d1e164.summary: Interprets this as not denying that sun and moon will shine, but that they will give no use of light to those in eternal bliss, since, as Jerome says, the office of heaven and earth, sun and moon will cease for us, and the Lord will be the light of his own forever.
claims: The blessed will not need the heavenly lights.

pl-l4d48c5-d1e173.summary: Adds that Isaiah may also be understood as saying sun and moon will not then rise and set as now.

pl-l4d48c5-d1e176.summary: Cites Isidore expounding Isaiah: after the judgment the sun will receive the reward of its labor and shine sevenfold, and neither sun nor moon will set, but stand in the order in which they were created, lest the impious, in torments under the earth, enjoy their light.
claims: Sun and moon will stand still after the judgment.

pl-l4d48c5-d1e186.summary: Cites Habakkuk: sun and moon stood in their order.

pl-l4d48c5-d1e192.summary: Notes that Isidore plainly says sun and moon will then shine but remain fixed, and also indicates that hell is under the earth.

pl-l4d48c5-d1e195.summary: Confesses that if asked what use the light of sun and moon will then have, he does not know, not remembering reading it in Scripture.
claims: The use of the heavenly lights after the judgment is unknown.

pl-l4d48c5.summary: At the Lord's coming the sun and moon are said to darken, not by losing their light but by a greater light, and the powers of heaven to be moved by wonder, not fear; before the day of judgment sun and moon will be eclipsed. In the new heaven and earth the moon will shine like the sun and the sun sevenfold, as in the first seven days before the fall, when their light was lessened by sin; there will be only day, as Zechariah says. Isaiah's saying that the sun will not shine for the blessed means it will be of no use to them, the Lord being their light, or that sun and moon will not rise and set but stand still, as Isidore and Habakkuk say, lest the damned below enjoy their light, which shows hell is under the earth. What use their light will then have Lombard confesses he does not know.
claims: At the judgment the heavenly lights are outshone, not extinguished.
After the judgment sun and moon will shine more brightly and stand still.
Their light was lessened by the first sin and will be restored.
The use of their light then is unknown.
